User: What are the evaluation criteria for the essays submitted to the contest, as determined by the panel of judges?: In celebration of dedicated service of 20 years, The Fountain magazine is sponsoring a Fountain Magazine Essay Writing Contest.
Cash prizes will be awarded to selected three winners who have written the best essay about the issues facing today’s immigrants.
Theme for Fountain Magazine Essay Writing Contest 2016:"Are you an immigrant, too? Were your parents or grandparents immigrants? Are we all immigrants in this world? How do immigrants contribute to your society? How do they cause problems in your society? How would you help immigrants thrive?"
Last year's theme was: “What do you think the theme of the 21st century will be- How do you think history will record the 21st century"
Fountain Magazine Essay Writing Contest is open to all writers across the World.
There is no age limit or a condition to fulfill for entry.
The contest is open to all who want to share his or her ideas with us.
The candidates have to fill in an Online Application Form available on the official website to submit the Essay.
On successfully filling the form, Essays must be submitted through the Essay Contest Page at https://www.fountainmagazine.com/essaycontest.
The candidates will be selected by the panel of judges who will select as per the literary effectiveness of the essay in reflecting the philosophy behind the motto, richness in content, and authenticity. All submitted essays will be evaluated using the following criteria.
Assistant: 1. Literary effectiveness: The judges will assess the essays based on the quality of writing, including style, tone, and structure. The use of language and the ability to engage the reader will also be considered.

2. Relevancy to the theme: The essay must address the theme of the contest and provide insights into the issues facing immigrants today. The essay should be relevant, informative, and thought-provoking.

3. Originality and creativity: Judges will look for essays that present a unique perspective on the theme, and that demonstrate creativity and innovation in the approach and arguments presented.

4. Clarity of thought: The essay should demonstrate a clear understanding of the theme, and the presentation of ideas should be coherent and well-articulated.

5. Richness in content: The essay should be well-researched and provide a rich and informative insight into the issues facing immigrants today. The essay should be factual, and the arguments should be well-supported by evidence and examples.

6. Authenticity: The essay should be the original work of the author and should not have been published or submitted for publication elsewhere.

7. Adherence to guidelines: The essay must adhere to the guidelines and instructions provided by the contest organizers. This includes word limit, formatting, and submission procedure.
User: Can you please remind me again how to submit my essay for the Fountain Magazine Essay Writing Contest?
Assistant: To submit your essay for the Fountain Magazine Essay Writing Contest, you need to follow these steps:

1. Go to the official website of the contest at https://www.fountainmagazine.com/essaycontest.

2. Fill out the Online Application Form available on the website.

3. Once you have filled out the form, click "Submit."

4. You will then be taken to the Essay Contest Page, where you can submit your essay.

5. Follow the instructions for formatting and submitting the essay as outlined on the page.

6. Make sure you have adhered to the guidelines and instructions provided by the contest organizers.

7. Once you have submitted your essay, the judges will evaluate it based on the criteria outlined on the contest's official website.

Good luck!
User: What is the current structure of the Naval Institute's essay contests, including the number of contests held each year, the types of prizes offered, and the eligibility requirements for participants? Answer according to: Almost from the earliest days of the Naval Institute, its essay contests have been one of its most important functions. The idea of having such an event was first proposed by Lieutenant Commander Allan D. Brown, USN, at the 9 May 1878 meeting of the Naval Institute. The Chair at the time, Commander Alfred Thayer Mahan, USN, Vice President of the Naval Institute, appointed as chairman of a committee Commander William T. Sampson, USN, to prepare a prize to be offered to the author of a paper deemed the best out of those submitted.
This action created the Naval Institute’s Prize Essay Contest. In 1948, the name changed to the General Prize Essay Contest. For the period of 1985–2007 the name changed to the Arleigh Burke Essay Contest to honor World War II hero and Cold War Navy CNO and Naval Institute President Admiral Arleigh Burke. From 2008–2013, the Naval Institute awarded General Prizes, but these went to authors of Proceedings articles judges as the best in a calendar year.
In 2014, the General Prize Essay Contest came back as generally envisioned by the Naval Institute’s founding fathers. Currently, the Naval Institute sponsors 14 essay contests a year.
The bottom line in all these essay contests is the Naval Institute remains committed to those authors who dare to write to advance the naval profession.
Note: All the essay contests include publication of the winning essays in Proceedings or Naval History magazine, recognition of the winners at a public event and cash prizes. Visit https://www.usni.org/essay-contests for specific details –– e.g., eligibility, word length, deadlines.

The essay contests are a long-standing tradition of the Naval Institute, with the first contest being proposed in 1878.

User: What are some creative ways to incorporate non-gaming aspects, such as food, music, or contests, into a LAN gaming party or event to increase engagement and socialization among attendees?
Assistant: 1. Host a potluck-style feast. Encourage attendees to bring their favorite food or drink to share with the group.

2. Set up a karaoke machine in a separate room. Allow attendees to sing their favorite tunes while others game.

3. Play music in the background. Create a playlist that has something for everyone, such as popular songs from different genres or decades.

4. Hold a costume contest. Encourage attendees to dress up as their favorite game characters, and award prizes for the best costumes.

5. Set up a photo booth. Create a fun space with props and a backdrop, and encourage attendees to take selfies and group photos.

6. Host a trivia competition. Create a list of questions related to games or pop culture, and award prizes for the attendees who answer the most correctly.

7. Hold a board game tournament. Set up a table for board games and let attendees compete with each other.

8. Organize a scavenger hunt. Create a list of clues and hide them around the venue. Encourage attendees to work together to find all the clues.

9. Host a cosplay competition. Encourage attendees to dress up as their favorite characters from games or anime, and award prizes for the best costumes.

10. Hold a raffle. Give attendees chances to win prizes by purchasing tickets, with proceeds going to a charity.

4. Gaming or tech gadgets, like a wireless charging pad, a drone, or a smartwatch.

- Review: "I absolutely adore this series! Set in a familiar time when things were different, Julie Mulhern manages to make each book a stand-alone success. There are twists and turns and lots of suspense that propel the reader forward. This book, in particular, was near and dear to my heart and so very well done."

2. The Nightingale: A Novel:
- Overall Rating: 5.0
- Review: "The Nightingale written by Kristin Hannah starts as an elderly widow realizes her life will likely be ending soon, and she is clearing out her house to prepare for the transition to a nursing home. Her son accompanies her in her Oregon coast home as she goes through her possessions. As she sorts through items in an old steamer trunk, she pulls out memories which lead her to share details from the past that her son had never been told. WWII, France, and the beginning of the Nazi occupation, two sisters Viann and Isabelle are presented situations that require extraordinary decisions. Each sister has a different approach to how they deal with the struggles of living in Nazi-occupied France. The story offers many believable insights into what life was like during this difficult time, keeping Jews from being identified and captured, assisting the French Resistance, and responding to the demands of an occupying army as they intern themselves and take what they want. Polly Stone is the reader of this Audiobook, and her voice is pleasant, yet somewhat unique, which adds character to the reading. She has a wide range of inflection and tempo, which captures your attention and keeps you listening. 14 CDs comprise over 17 hours of narration for a 450-page book. Polly provides each character their own style, and before long, you can easily identify all the participants in the story. The story..."

3. Special Circumstances:
- Overall Rating: 4.0
- Review: "Enjoyable story with smarmy characters enough to shock most readers. Lots of twists and turns. Mike Daley, as it turns out in this book, is one of the few ethical lawyers left."
